name: Director (VL)
hook: The car that ended Peter Brock's partnership with Holden came with an optional box of crystal and magnets.
story: Peter Brock was Australia's favourite racing driver. He won Bathurst again and again in Holdens. His own company turned Commodores into fast road cars that carried his signature. Then, in 1986, Brock showed off a small black box. Inside sat a sliver of crystal ringed by magnets. He called it the Energy Polarizer. He said it worked by "aligning the molecules" of the car. No test ever showed it doing a thing. Holden wanted nothing to do with it. Brock would not back down. He also planned an independent rear end borrowed from Opel, which Holden thought was not tested enough. On 20 February 1987 he launched his new flagship anyway. It was the Director, and the box cost an extra 480 dollars. Within days, Holden withdrew all support. A group of sceptics had already handed Brock their Bent Spoon award for the gadget. So here is a big V8 sedan shaped by one man's belief. It is also the car that cost him his partner.
description: The HDT Director was the last flagship of HDT Special Vehicles, Peter Brock's road-car company, before Holden cut its ties with him. Based on the VL Commodore, it used a 4,987 cc version of Holden's locally built V8 rated at 177 kW. A handful got independent rear suspension sourced from Opel. Buyers could add the Energy Polarizer for AU$480, a crystal-and-magnet device with no proven effect. Holden withdrew its support days after the February 1987 launch.
